## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `Security`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `security-configurations`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **Security**.

## Step 2: Configure security

1. <!-- manual: Open your integration from the project home. -->
2. On the integration overview page, select **Configure Security** in the top-right panel.
3. <!-- manual: In the Configure Security panel, select the endpoint you want to secure from the Endpoints dropdown. -->
4. <!-- manual: Enable the security schemes you want to apply: -->
5. <!-- manual: API Key — Check the API Key checkbox. You can edit the security header name if your client uses a different header. -->
6. <!-- manual: OAuth2 — Check the OAuth2 checkbox. You can edit the security header name if your client uses a different header, but it must support Bearer tokens. -->
7. <!-- manual: If you want the authenticated user's identity to be forwarded to your backend service, enable Pass end-user attributes to upstream. -->
8. <!-- manual: To assign OAuth2 scopes to specific resources: 1. In the Permissions List panel, click Add Permission (Scope). 2. In the Add Permission dialog, select the required scope and click + Add New. 3. In the Resources list, expand the resource you want to restrict. 4. Click Permission (Scopes) dropdown and select the desired scopes. 5. Add the required scopes and assign them to the resource. -->
9. <!-- manual: You can also disable security for specific resources by turning the Security toggle off for that resource. -->
10. Once you have configured the security settings as needed, click **Apply** to save the changes.

## Step 3: API Key

1. In the integration overview, select **Developer Portal**.
2. <!-- manual: Subscribe to the API by selecting or creating an application. -->
3. <!-- manual: In your application, click Generate Key under the API Key column. -->
4. <!-- manual: Copy the generated key and include it in the configured security header of your requests: -->
